metadata.explanation: Exact dataset support was found for oxidation of the corresponding Boc-protected amino alcohol to the aldehyde; the precursor also gave an exact stock hit. Experimental feasibility still requires condition screening.

Alternative first cut is Boc protection of aminoacetaldehyde. Validation found class compatibility and atom-inventory consistency but no dataset or trusted-template support; both precursors are therefore left as non-stock unresolved leaves.

Direct substitution of the aryl fluoride para to the aldehyde by morpholine. Atom inventory and reaction-class compatibility passed validation, but no exact dataset reaction or trusted template supported this specific step; experimental feasibility therefore remains uncertain.

Proposed substitution of the activated aryl fluoride by morpholine gives the amino benzyl alcohol. This second-step cut is a mechanistic proposal without exact hidden-dataset support; the aryl alcohol precursor is left as a non-stock leaf because no exact stock confirmation was obtained.

Oxidation of the corresponding primary benzyl alcohol furnishes the aldehyde. Atom inventory and reaction-class compatibility passed validation, but hidden evidence did not support this exact conversion.
metadata.reaction_class: oxidation of primary alcohol to aldehyde

metadata.explanation: Validated exact dataset-supported Williamson ether formation from the stock phenol and 1,4-dibromobutane, retaining one terminal bromide for the next step.
Validated exact dataset-supported N-alkylation of the secondary arylpiperazine with the primary bromide intermediate; experimental feasibility still requires confirmation.

Alternative first cut at the aryl ether suggests direct Williamson coupling of the stock phenol with the aminoalkyl halide. Validation found atom balance and class compatibility but no exact dataset or trusted-template support, so this route is lower confidence and incomplete pending sourcing of the halide.

N-sulfonylation of the cyanoindole with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride. Validation passed with exact dataset support (CEUFGDDOMXCXFW-UHFFFAOYSA-N.YYROPELSRYBVMQ-UHFFFAOYSA-N>>OIWHUFPOHDKMFT-UHFFFAOYSA-N).
Reduce the aryl nitrile to the primary aminomethyl group. Disconnection validation passed with exact dataset support (OIWHUFPOHDKMFT-UHFFFAOYSA-N>>JHRFJDRMDHBZPF-UHFFFAOYSA-N).
Reduce the stock cyanoindole to the corresponding aminomethyl indole; this is the same nitrile-to-primary-amine bond transformation supported exactly on the N-tosyl analogue in the first route.

Late-stage N-sulfonylation of the aminomethyl indole with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride. The cut is chemically standard and passed structure, inventory, leakage, and class checks, but no exact dataset reaction or trusted template was found; experimental chemoselectivity between indole N and the primary amine must therefore be established.
